meta.source: Rinnai America Corporation, tankless water heater model chart and specifications (2016), hosted by Lowe's; Noritz, How to Size a Tankless (printable, 2024); Lochinvar, Tankless Water Heater Sizing Guide
meta.notes: Manufacturer figures used two ways: the gas input sizes in the size chart, and the cross-check of our formula against the flow each manufacturer publishes. The Rinnai chart gives an Energy Factor (the rating used before UEF); newer models of the same size are rated in UEF and are very close. Cross-check and chart settings below that are not manufacturer figures are labelled as Hot Water Math choices. publishedRisesF = the two temperature rises Rinnai's chart publishes flow for (gpmAt70, gpmAt50).

sizeChart.source: Gas input sizes are the residential input ratings in the Rinnai chart above; the rises are a Hot Water Math display choice covering warm to very cold inlet water. Electric sizes come from data/electrical.json.

examples.label: 4 showers and a dishwasher
examples.pick: a pair of units (EZ98, NRC98, NRCR92 or NR98)

noritzExample.source: Noritz, How to Size a Tankless (printable V1, 2024), steps 1 to 3

lochinvarCheck.note: Lochinvar sizing guide: capacity in showers at 50 °F and 70 °F incoming water with a 120 °F setpoint, and a GPM by temperature rise chart per model. Used as a qualitative check on the per-shower rule (one shower per about 2.5 GPM).
lochinvarCheck.source: Lochinvar, Tankless Water Heater Sizing Guide

rules.source: Hot Water Math editorial threshold (docs/STRATEGY.md §3.2): warn that a single whole-house electric unit is rarely enough when the rise is above 60 °F and the flow is above 4 GPM

pointOfUse.source: Eemax ProAdvantage single-module electric tankless specifications (distributor copy of the Eemax spec sheet): PA004120T 3.5 kW 120 V 29 A 10 AWG; PA005240T 4.8 kW 240 V 20 A 10 AWG; PA007240T 6.5 kW 240 V 27 A 10 AWG; PA010240T 9.5 kW 240 V 40 A 8 AWG; PA012240T 11.5 kW 240 V 48 A 6 AWG (checked 2026-11-14). Showers need more power than these, so the point-of-use mode also looks at the whole-house Rheem units in data/electrical.json.

sizingCheck.example: EEM12004 (3.5 kW, 120 V): 0.5 GPM at 52 °F inlet, output 105 °F, one hand-washing sink; "Do not use" below 52 °F inlet
sizingCheck.source: Eemax Sizing Guide: "kW Required = GPM x (temp rise/6.83)", "kW reference is based on a 100% heater efficiency"; EEM12004 spec sheet: "GALLONS PER MINUTE (GPM) BASED ON OUPUT WATER TEMPERATURE OF 105°F", 52 °F inlet: 0.5 GPM (checked 2026-11-14)

sandwich.source: Eemax (a Rheem company), Cure for the Cold Water Sandwich white paper
sandwich.quote: It takes about 10 seconds for the ignition sequence in most gas heaters to restart, and this is when cold water is introduced into the home's hot water system.
sandwich.fix: Integrating the Mini Tank into the hot water outlet of a gas tankless heater (as indicated in the diagram below) removes the Cold Water Sandwich Effect.

recirculation.quote: If your home does not have a dedicated return line, select Rinnai tankless water heaters can offer faster hot water without adding an additional cold return line.
recirculation.how: A thermal by-pass valve added to the cold water line helps ensure recirculation is enabled
